transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm a kindergarten teacher, and... what brings me in is that the second I spot balloons at school, even if they're all the way across the hallway, my chest just tightens up. I kind of freeze for a moment before I can even think clearly about what I’m supposed to be doing.
Do you ever experience these sudden feelings of panic or chest tightness completely out of the blue, when there is no obvious trigger around?
No, it's really just when I see them. I don't get that feeling out of nowhere. It's always tied to the balloons.
Did this intense reaction start after a particularly frightening or traumatic experience involving balloons?

Yes, it did actually. It started about seven months ago. We were having a children’s art celebration at the school, and a balloon burst right close to my face. Ever since that happened, I've had this reaction.
Do you find yourself actively going out of your way to avoid balloons or situations where they might be present?

Yes, I do. Lately, I've been... well, asking my aides to handle the birthday circles for me. Or I'll just move away from any festival tables that have balloons nearby. If I absolutely have to stay in the area, I just keep my distance. I really just focus on getting through it without looking at them.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of cue-induced acute anxiety and freezing response to balloons suggests specific phobia, panic disorder, or trauma-related avoidance.
